_comment: Tier-2 for dune::poisson_mms#2 — what an under-integrated error norm actually does. EXECUTED 2026-08-06 against dune-fem 2.12.0.2 in the dune-fem-env conda env (the runner needs DUNE_PYTHON=~/miniconda3/envs/dune-fem-env/bin/python; there is no ofa-dune env on this host). The claim marks itself 'theory-derived; not provoked live on this install' and predicts 'EOCs that DRIFT AWAY from k+1 as levels refine (error floor)'. Provoked live, THE PREDICTED FLOOR DOES NOT HAPPEN. One Lagrange-order-2 solve per level on the MMS u* = sin(pi x) sin(pi y) + 0.3 x^2 y, levels n = 4, 8, 16, 32, with the SAME uh measured at quadrature orders 0, 2 and 2k+4 = 8 so nothing but the error norm changes between columns. Printed EOCs: q=8 gives 2.9788 / 2.9950 / 2.9988 (theory 3); q=2 gives 2.9850 / 2.9966 / 2.9992; q=0 gives 3.6793 / 3.9294 / 3.9829. Every column keeps converging to the finest level — no stall, no floor — and the drift that does occur is UPWARD: the degree-0 rule samples the error where it superconverges and reports order 4, which reads as 'better than theory' rather than as a defect. What under-integration really costs is a BIAS in the error constant that survives refinement: relative to the well-integrated norm, q=2 over-reports by +0.4024 / +0.3965 / +0.3949 / +0.3946 (essentially fixed) while q=0 under-reports by -0.9743 / -0.9842 / -0.9917 / -0.9958, i.e. the reported error is up to 240x too SMALL and gets relatively worse as the mesh refines. The optimistic direction is the hazard: an error two orders of magnitude too small with an order that looks better than theory is exactly what a convergence gate exists to catch and exactly what it would wave through. CROSS-CHECK at Lagrange order 3 (levels 4, 8, 16, measured but not gated, to keep the fixture cheap): q=0 there OVER-reports by a steady +120.6% / +121.6% / +121.8% and gives order 4 — so the sign of the low-order bias depends on k, while 'a persistent bias, never a floor' holds in both. MUTATION EVIDENCE: feeding the same checker the behaviour the claim predicts — the under-integrated columns stalling on a 1e-5 error floor while the well-integrated one keeps order 3 — made the fixture print no_error_floor_at_any_quadrature_order=False, lowest_order_norm_reports_better_than_theory=False, lowest_order_norm_under_reports_the_error=False and under_integration_biases_the_norm_it_does_not_floor_it=False, emit four FAIL: lines, drop the OK sentinel and return 2. dune.grid / dune.fem are imported at module scope, so without DUNE the process dies on import and the runner records a failure, never a pass. MUTATION CONTROL (2026-08-07): T2_MUTATE=1 raises the LOWEST quadrature order under test from 0 to 2*order+6, removing the under-integration while leaving everything else. Unmutated the fixture still PASSES; mutated it FAILS because the expectations 'lowest_order_norm_reports_better_than_theory=True', 'lowest_order_norm_under_reports_the_error=True', 'under_integration_biases_the_norm_it_does_not_floor_it=True', 'dune_mms_error_quadrature_gate=OK' are no longer printed and the forbidden token 'FAIL:' appears. Re-verify with `cd <fixture dir> && T2_MUTATE=1 ~/miniconda3/envs/dune-fem-env/bin/python source.py` (the mutation branch lives in source.py, so the proof is one command and needs no external harness).
